text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The opposition accuses the government of creating a political impasse in the country by refusing to dialogue with other political stakeholders.
- The British High Commission says Zambian exports to Britain have reached a record $30 million a year.
- The ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD) suspends a provincial minister in northern Zambia for allegedly causing divisions in the party.
- Operations at the University of Zambia are paralysed as unionised workers strike to demand the payment of salary arrears dating back to January.
- Defence minister Ben Mwila faces dismissal for purportedly campaigning to suceed president Frederick Chiluba after the president banned such campaigns as premature.
- Vice president Godfrey Miyanda urges Southern African Development Community (SADC) member states to promote free media in their countries.
